close_reason: Landed commit 4596a69. MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes trait rustdoc now carries an explicit '# Unknown account_id' paragraph documenting the SHOULD-return-Ok-empty-ChangesResult convention. The in-tree handle_metadata_changes handler validates account existence via JmapBackend::account_exists BEFORE invoking this method (bd:JMAP-826m.34) and surfaces accountNotFound itself; downstream consumers calling the trait directly therefore do not need to repeat the check, but they MUST behave gracefully if invoked with an unknown account. The reference MemoryBackend follows the empty-Ok convention naturally (change-log lookup falls through to an empty slice). Returning Err is technically valid but surfaces at the wire as serverFail rather than accountNotFound — which is the hard-to-debug failure mode the bead flagged. The same paragraph belongs on the upstream JmapBackend::get_changes (and the 4 other JmapBackend read methods) — filed as bd:JMAP-qzvb (P4). Once that lands, the canonical-template rule will propagate the foundation paragraph to other extension-server backend traits' analogous methods. Quality gates: cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, doc -D warnings green.
description:
backend.rs:137 — the default impl of MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes delegates to self.get_changes::<Metadata>(...). The trait doc focuses on §3.3 filter-arg semantics (what is filtered, when state advances) but is silent on:

- Does the trait method validate that account_id exists, or is that the caller's responsibility?
- If account_id does not exist, does the trait method return Ok(empty ChangesResult) or Err(BackendChangesError::Other(...)) or Err(NoSuchAccount)?
- The handler (metadata.rs:104-111) does its own account_exists() check before calling, so the in-tree caller is fine. But a downstream consumer calling the trait method directly (e.g. for cross-method composition or for testing) has no documented behavior to rely on.

The reference MemoryBackend override at memory.rs:835 silently returns an empty result for an unknown account (the change_log entry lookup returns None, .unwrap_or(&[])). A naive override that asserts account_exists() first would diverge — both are reasonable, neither is contract.

Recommendation:
- Document in MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes rustdoc: 'When account_id does not exist, the default impl delegates to JmapBackend::get_changes which is itself unspecified for unknown accounts. Backends overriding this method SHOULD return Ok(empty ChangesResult) for unknown accounts to match the in-tree handler's expectation (the handler validates account existence before this call and treats trait-level errors as serverFail).' The same paragraph belongs in the JmapBackend::get_changes upstream rustdoc — file a follow-up bead against jmap-server if appropriate.

What goes wrong if this stays:
- A backend implementor copying the canonical pattern but adding stricter account validation will produce a different error class than the handler expects, surfacing as serverFail instead of accountNotFound at the wire. Hard to debug without reading the handler source.
title: API: MetadataBackend::get_metadata_changes default impl — account validation responsibility unspecified
